findings.claim: [docs/2026-11-13-rent-vs-buy-design.md, section 7, the DLM bullet that replaced the reproduced Table 2 figures] - DLM's Table 2 (`sources/dlm_roiw_2008-13.txt`): census net rents against the BLS rent index, and census average prices against Freddie Mac's repeat-sales index, decade by decade.
findings.evidence:
S: I checked the bullet against the stored article. sources/dlm_roiw_2008-13.txt:230-231 is Table 2, 'BLS Tenant Rent Index and CMHPI vs. DCH Benchmarks'. Its columns (:234-265) are 'Net Rents, DCH', 'BLS Rent Index*' and their difference, then 'Average Prices, DCH', 'CMHPI*' and their difference, each in annual percent change. The rows are four decades (:282-290). The notes (:293-294) say that growth runs decade to decade, that the BLS index is 'Rent of Primary Residence', and that CMHPI starts in 1970. :341-342 calls CMHPI 'the repeat-sales house price index published by Freddie Mac'. Each clause of the bullet matches.

Primary document and reference: my copy of sources/dlm_roiw_2008-13.pdf hashes to 5d94feb5...dbaed, as Appendix B records (audit :1032, http://www.roiw.org/2008/2008-13.pdf). pdftotext re-extracts it byte for byte as the stored .txt. It is the journal's typeset article (Review of Income and Wealth, Series 54, Number 2, June 2008; printed pages 279 to 284 over 6 PDF pages; embedded DOI 10.1111/j.1475-4991.2008.00274.x), and it matches the post's entry at draft :122 in authors, year, title, volume, issue, pages and DOI. The bullet now holds no cell: dlm_scan.py and dlm_scan_t1.py find no run of Table 1 or Table 2 cells in any committed text file.

Notes: the bullet does not say the columns are growth rates, which is acceptable for a pointer. sources/ is not committed (.gitignore:17), as README.md's 'Run it' section and data/README.md:5 state, and Appendix B gives the PDF's address. | L: design :378-379. sources/dlm_roiw_2008-13.txt:230-298 is DLM's Table 2. Its top half sets average net rents from the Decennial Census of Housing against the BLS rent index; the note at :294 names it as Rent of Primary Residence. Its bottom half sets census average prices against the CMHPI, which :341 calls the repeat-sales house price index published by Freddie Mac. The rows run 1960-70 to 1990-2000, and the note at :293 gives decade-to-decade growth, Q2 to Q2. So the paraphrase is accurate and states no figure. A diff of the pre-round-2 copy (p30r2/lens-K/rebuild, 21:27:57) against the current design shows the bullet replaced the seven Difference cells of Table 2 (txt :249-252 and :276-279). A grep of the committed files finds 0 copies of that run. Of Table 1's levels, only one individual attributed figure remains, at audit :110. Context: section 6 says the predictions rest on the inputs seen during the vet (section 7), and the bullet still records that Table 2 was seen. Note: the path names the derived .txt extract in the git-ignored sources/, which Appendix B does not list (audit :17-19). README.md:28 says stored documents are not in the repository, and the design names the article as Davis, Lehnert and Martin (2008) at :116 and :461, so a GitHub reader can still find the table. | H: design :378-379. Table 2 of the stored article (sources/dlm_roiw_2008-13.txt:230-288) sets the annual percent change of census (DCH) average net rents beside the BLS rent index (the notes at :294 name it as Rent of Primary Residence). It also sets census average prices beside the CMHPI, decade by decade from 1960-70 to 1990-2000, with no CMHPI value for 1960-70. Lines :341-342 describe the CMHPI as Freddie Mac's repeat-sales index. So the bullet describes the table's two comparisons and its decade grain. The vet read this table (draft/vet-values-seen.txt:272 and :479 name DLM's Table 2), so it belongs in section 7. My run scanner finds no DLM Table 2 run in any committed file. It is sensitive: it does find the old bullet's runs in the round 2 copy of the design, at :378 and :380. Note: sources/ is git-ignored (.gitignore:17), so for a reader of the repository the path points to a local file. README.md:28 says the stored documents are not in the repository, and the article is in the design's references (:116, :461), so the table can still be found. | K: sources/dlm_roiw_2008-13.txt:230-290 holds DLM's Table 2, in rows 1960-70 to 1990-2000. The top half sets average net rent growth from the decennial census (DCH) against the BLS rent index (the note names 'Rent of Primary Residence'). The bottom half sets DCH average price growth against the CMHPI, which the text (:340-341) calls Freddie Mac's repeat-sales index. The bullet's description matches. The bullet reproduces no figure. My scanner (lens-K/dlm_runs.py, ordered runs of 3 or more cells of every Table 1 and Table 2 column) finds 0 hits in the 19 committed text files. On the stored article and the pre-round-2 design it finds 14 hits, so it is sensitive. Notes: the CMHPI column is NA for 1960-70 (the index starts 1970:1); 'decade by decade' describes the rows and does not claim every cell. The pointer targets a git-ignored text extract (.gitignore:17). That fits Appendix B's own rule, which leaves derived extracts unlisted (audit :943-944) and lists the PDF at :1032. It is the design's only sources/ pointer. Nothing in the draft or the audit relied on the withdrawn figures: grep finds no 'Table 2' for DLM and no 'outgrew'.

findings.evidence:
S: The 24 files are exactly what 'git ls-files --others --exclude-standard rent-vs-buy' lists. I scanned them against the raw files with my own scripts (p30r4/lens-S/scripts), and each scan finds a planted control. Third-party cells are cited here by locator only.
- AEI 'rent-price data' (aei_scan2.py): no run of 3 or more successive rows in any of the 19 committed text files. results_scan.py finds 0 of results.json's 14,398 floats within 1e-9 of any of the 1,392 cells, as is, x100 or /100.
- ICI (ici_scan.py, every column and row of every sheet): only coincidences with hand-typed constants (build_analysis.py:46, test_rentbuy.py:160). results.json holds no S3 column E value /100, and as is only coincidences in rules.sell_share.
- French monthly factors: no run of 4 or more months in the text files. In results.json the only successive match is inputs.property_tax.by_year 1985 to 1989 against RF values of 0.01, a coincidence.
- DLM paper: no run of Table 1 or Table 2 cells; one attributed Table 1 average at provenance-audit.md:110.
- NAIC: comma-formatted tokens from the three report texts match only individual figures (the form totals at provenance-audit.md:453) and coincidences ('$1,000 value', cell counts, model dollar amounts). The six cells at the locators r3:item:4 kept (2023 text :12040, :12060, :12794, :12812; 2022 :12782; 2021 :10314, all on Table 4 pages) appear in none of the 20 committed text files, in comma, plain or integer form.
- The vet-file cells at draft/vet-values-seen.txt :72, :91, :740 and :797 (113 tokens of 3 or more digits) appear in neither round record.

Rights basis:
- Freddie Mac: the PMMS page (sources/fm_pmms_ia20261112180833.txt:221) and the weekly workbook's note (sharedStrings item 16) both say information 'may be used with proper attribution' and prohibit alteration. Section 7's annual averages come from the discontinued annual table (the vet's copy of Internet Archive capture 20220531200035, p30data/mortgage-verify/dl-41, sha256 9c837f5c...). That file carries the same note, and its 'Annual Avgs:' row matches section 7's nine rates at the file's 0.00 display.
- AEI's terms (aei_AEI-Housing-Terms-of-Use_ia20220319235839.txt:71-73) grant no licence to reproduce or distribute, and the workbook is ignored (.gitignore:3).
- The NAIC reports forbid reproduction without written permission (naic2023 text :62-63).
- I opened charts 1 to 4: model output only, with credits.

Notes:
(1) The locator 'provenance-audit.md:74-76', used here and twice in round3-verdicts.json, is off. Lines :74-75 are the PMMS FAQ bullet, and the permission sentence runs over :76-77. The cited range ends before 'allow use with attribution'.
(2) ICI's permission (sources/ici_copyright_linking_ia20260514103053.txt:682) asks for 'Investment Company Institute as the source and http://www.ici.org as the URL'. The design names 'ICI' and the report at :90, with no URL, while giving ICI values at :390-391 and :244. data/README.md:342 and the post's reference (draft :138) carry the URL, so the README statements about the post hold, and 'attributed' holds in its ordinary sense. Adding the URL to the design would be an addition, so it is the owner's call. | L: (a) Files.
